title: Treat verification-suite efficiency as repository entropy
body:
## Outcome

Make the work-suggestion pipeline consistently detect and propose evidence-backed improvements to verification-suite wall time and signal density as repository entropy. This should cover safe parallelization, avoidable serialization or setup, and obsolete, redundant, or superseded tests without weakening the repository's unique behavioral, platform, failure-mode, or contract evidence.

## Why this matters

Verification is a recurring delivery bottleneck and naturally accumulates entropy as the product and harness evolve. The current suggestion workflow inspects tests and performance, but its `tests` category is defined around missing feedback while non-behavioral code quality only partially covers duplicate cleanup. Neither contract explicitly audits the verification critical path or whether expensive tests still add a distinct observable claim.

## Acceptance criteria

- Verification-suite efficiency is modeled explicitly within the entropy-review and work-suggestion pipeline, with a bounded category contract or equivalent reviewed policy representation. Existing projects are not silently opted into broader refill behavior.
- Ordinary execution may record one compact incidental observation when current work exposes verification inefficiency, but it never pauses to run a repository-wide suite audit. Explicit entropy review remains the route for a broader audit.
- Suggestions use observed evidence such as repeated component timings, the CI dependency graph, setup/fixture reuse, test ownership, and the distinct observable claims covered by candidate tests. Expensive suites are not run merely to generate ideas.
- The audit can identify safe parallelization or sharding, unnecessary serialization, duplicated expensive setup, obsolete tests, superseded tests, and tests that provide no distinct useful signal. Shared implementation methods or fixtures alone never prove redundancy.
- A proposed removal, merge, or replacement must preserve unique behavior, boundaries, platforms, supported runtimes, failure semantics, integration contracts, and regression evidence. Uncertain evidence produces a measurement or harness goal rather than deletion.
- Performance comparisons distinguish CI critical-path wall time from aggregate compute cost and use repeated, noise-aware measurements. The workflow does not introduce flaky hard-duration gates or hide races and resource contention through parallelism.
- Dry-run remains read-only, apply requires explicit authority, and exhausted-queue refill honors the reviewed category list and cap. Compatibility behavior for existing reviewed policies is deterministic and tested.
- Focused workflow, policy, entropy-inbox, and suggestion tests prove positive detection, rejection of unsafe test trimming, policy gating, and preservation of the canonical cross-platform verification contract. User-facing documentation explains the new entropy concern plainly.

## Scope and non-goals

This goal covers the entropy category model, suggestion guidance, reviewed policy defaults and compatibility, incidental observation routing, focused tests, documentation, and any small measurement interface needed to make suggestions honest. It may use this repository's validation graph as a proving fixture. It does not weaken required CI, remove tests solely because they touch the same methods, optimize arbitrary product runtime, automatically rewrite test suites, or establish a universal wall-time threshold.

## Relationships and first probe

Completed #364 supplies privacy-safe workflow timing concepts, #205 avoids exact local/CI duplication, and #326 reduced mechanically redundant human acceptance work. This goal complements them by governing ongoing verification-suite entropy rather than duplicating their outcomes.

First probe: inventory every component of the canonical validation graph, record repeated component and critical-path timings, and map the slowest candidates to their unique observable claims. Attempt to identify at least one safe parallelization opportunity and one apparently redundant test, then falsify both candidates by checking platform, input, failure-mode, and contract differences before designing the category contract.

## Implementation dependency and release acceptance

User-approved queue revision (2026-09-15): depend on completed implementation goal #383 instead of parent #380. The dedicated entropy-review implementation is integrated and verified; the pending full human acceptance journey is a release gate, not a prerequisite for this feature work. Run focused automated checks and required CI for this change. The final integrated journey remains tracked by #384 after #379 and #390 finish.
